If afternoon hyperglycemia persists (peak BG >140 mg/dL), increase afternoon basal by additional 0.05–0.1 U/h. If evening hypoglycemia recurs, reduce evening basal by 0.05 U/h. Target: afternoon BG peak <130 mg/dL, evening TBR <3%.
meal_suggestion: Observed user strategy is Reactive Correction with SMB/UAM Micro-Dosing, no prebolus, no meal-bolus calculation. User delivers 0.1–0.2 U micro-corrections at meal start (not prebolus) and relies on basal + SMB + UAM to manage carb absorption. No meals are logged; no e-carbs are entered. Strategy is safe (TIR 86%) and prevents hypoglycemia during meal phase (SMB gated by inferred COB). Afternoon meals (lunch ~50–60 g, hour 12–16) result in elevated BG 140–160 mg/dL for 4 hours; evening meals well-controlled. Root cause of afternoon hyperglycemia is NOT bolus strategy; it is basal insufficiency (basal 0.7 U/h weak for postprandial period when SMB is gated). Do not change bolus strategy now. After basal is tuned and afternoon BG reduced to 100–130 mg/dL range, user could optionally trial 10–15 min prebolus for lunch to further reduce peak BG, or begin logging meals to enable bolus calculator and validate CR. Adding e-carbs is not recommended at this time; focus on basal first.
primary_rec_title: Strengthen afternoon basal (10:00–15:59) and eliminate evening basal valley (16:00–17:59) to address concurrent hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia clustering.
summary: User is achieving 86% time-in-range on AAPS with SMB/UAM enabled, correction-only bolus strategy, and no meal carb entries. Data quality is excellent (98.7% CGM coverage). Overnight control is stable (basal 0.6–0.8 U/h well-tuned for 90 mg/dL target). Afternoon hyperglycemia (10:00–16:00 hours local: avg 132–162 mg/dL, TAR 7.5–32.1%) and evening hypoglycemia clustering (17:00–19:00: TBR 7.7%, documented lows 41–48 mg/dL on 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-14) are the primary pattern concerns. Root cause analysis points to basal schedule mismatch in afternoon and early evening, compounded by flat ISF (56 mg/dL/U) that does not account for GLP-1 effect variability (effective ISF observed 19–80 mg/dL/U across dataset). Automation (SMB/UAM/Dynamic ISF) is well-configured and functioning appropriately; it is compensating for profile insufficiency, not causing dyscontrol. No meal boluses or carb entries are recorded; user relies entirely on basal + SMB/UAM + temperature basals to manage eating. Overall risk is moderate: system is safe and stable most of the time, but recurring afternoon hyperglycemia and evening hypo clustering present a tuning opportunity.

profile_rec_text: Increase basal rate 10:00–16:00 from 0.7 to 0.8 U/h. Monitor for 3–5 days. If afternoon time-in-range improves to >80% and hypoglycemia does not increase, change is supported. Do not change other basal segments; overnight/evening are adequate.
meal_suggestion: Small immediate bolus (~10–20% of expected meal+correction insulin, typically 0.1–0.35 U for standard meals) followed by aggressive SMB every 3 minutes (delivering 80–90% of meal insulin via automation). No prebolus (carbs not logged in advance); reactive bolusing at meal recognition via UAM glucose-rise detection (≥8 mg/dL/5 min). No e-carbs declared or logged; all meals treated as simple rapid-carb. This strategy is operationally aligned with AAPS configuration (UAM-only, carb logging absent) but creates IOB-stacking vulnerability when meals are frequent (<4 hours apart) or when corrective boluses are given hours after meal events without checking IOB.
primary_rec_title: Increase basal rate 10:00–16:00 window from 0.7 to 0.8 U/h to address primary afternoon hyperglycemia driver
summary: 14-day Nightscout telemetry (98.7% CGM coverage, 3,995 glucose entries, zero carb logs) shows 86% time-in-range with recurrent afternoon hyperglycemia (10:00–17:00 local, peaks 285–293 mg/dL) and two hypoglycemia clusters (Aug 13–14, Aug 21 early). AAPS automation (SMB, UAM, Dynamic ISF) is configured correctly and actively functioning but cannot overcome an underlying profile insufficiency. Basal rate 0.7–0.8 U/h in the 10:00–16:00 window is likely insufficient; this is the primary driver of afternoon highs. Meal bolus strategy inferred from telemetry is small immediate bolus (~10–20%) + SMB-heavy (80–90% of meal insulin), with no prebolus, no e-carbs, and no carb logging. This strategy aligns with AAPS defaults but creates IOB stacking risk when meals are frequent or corrective boluses follow high-carb events. No changes to automation settings are recommended; focus should be sequential profile tuning (basal), then resumption of carb logging, then meal-strategy review.

profile_rec_text: Raise ISF from 56 to 110 mg/dL/U as primary profile change. Implement immediately (or within 1 day), monitor for 3–5 days, then evaluate basal 10:00–16:00 change. Do not raise max_basal or max_IOB; do not change targets, SMB settings, or Dynamic ISF adjustment factor concurrently.
meal_suggestion: User is currently employing a reactive, automation-supplemented meal coverage model. No declared prebolus; boluses are given at or after meal time (glucose elevated). Immediate bolus percentage is 100% (instantaneous). User manual boluses are weak in absolute terms (0.05–0.45 U typical) but proportional to profile ISF 56; after ISF is corrected to 110, user boluses will proportionally increase (e.g., 0.1 U becomes 0.2 U for same carb amount), requiring no behavior change. AAPS SMB/UAM supplements user boluses with 0.3–1.6 U per meal, detecting unannounced meals via glucose rise (UAM mechanism). E-carbs are not used (zero meal logs; zero e-carb entries). Overall strategy works for closed-loop automation but relies heavily on system responsiveness and creates cumulative IOB (0.5–2 U afternoon+evening) that causes evening lows. Recommended action: (1) Raise ISF 56→110 immediately; user boluses will auto-increase proportionally; (2) Monitor 3–5 days; AAPS SMB/UAM will auto-adjust downward as user boluses become more adequate; (3) Restore carb logging for ≥3 days to validate CR (11–13 g/U) and assess meal sizes (confirm breakfast 30–50g, lunch 50–80g, dinner 30–50g); (4) After basal/ISF stabilized with carb logs, consider (a) adding 10–15 min prebolus to reduce afternoon peak and SMB reliance, and (b) conditional e-carbs for GLP-1 days if lunch absorption delayed. Current reactive model is acceptable short-term while AAPS automation fills gaps, but optimal control would benefit from proactive prebolus and carb logging.
primary_rec_title: Raise ISF from 56 to 110 mg/dL/U
summary: User is on AAPS closed-loop (SMB/UAM enabled, Dynamic ISF 70%) with a 14-day CGM record showing 86% TIR overall but significant afternoon hyperglycemia (32.1% above range in hour 16 local) and evening lows (15.3% below range in hour 19 local). Zero carbohydrate entries are logged despite inferred meal consumption (breakfast, lunch, dinner pattern evident from glucose and bolus records). All therapy is labeled correction boluses; no meal boluses are recorded separately. Manual boluses are under-dosed (0.05–0.45 U typical for inferred 30–80g carbs), and AAPS SMB/UAM compensates with 0.3–1.6 U per meal. The profile shows ISF 56 mg/dL/U (uniform, too low vs. observed therapy responses of 80–890), basal 0.6–0.8 U/h daytime (insufficient for 10:00–16:00 window), and adequate DIA (10 h). No meal strategy is declared by user; strategy is inferred entirely from telemetry. Primary issues are basal insufficiency (10:00–16:00), ISF underestimation (56 vs. 100–120 needed), and meal logging absence (blocking CR and e-carb validation). Secondary issues are weak user bolusing (reactive, not preventive) and afternoon IOB accumulation causing evening lows. The primary recommendation is to raise ISF from 56 to 110 mg/dL/U and increase basal 10:00–16:00 from 0.7 to 0.85 U/h, then monitor and re-assess automation behavior. Meal logging must be restored to finalize CR and meal strategy.

profile_rec_text: Do not change profile settings at this time. All basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA segments are individually reasonable and supported by telemetry. Afternoon glucose peaks (hour 14–16: 148–293 mg/dL) and severe lows (08-13, 08-14: 41–51 mg/dL) are not due to profile defects; they are due to meal bolus timing/sizing strategy (minimal immediate bolus, SMB lag) and correction bolus oversizing during high IOB. The profile will function correctly once meal bolus strategy is normalized and meal logging is introduced. Profile changes now would introduce risk without addressing the root cause (meal dosing). Verify meal bolus strategy (prebolus consistency, immediate bolus ≥20% of total) and establish correction bolus limits before considering profile tuning.
meal_suggestion: Establish a consistent meal bolus strategy: deliver 20–30% of expected meal insulin immediately at meal start (prebolus 0–15 minutes before), and let SMB/UAM deliver remaining 70–80% as micro-boluses over 2–4 hours post-meal. Without meal logs, SMB/UAM remain the safety-net dosing mechanism; immediate bolus reduces their burden and improves peak glucose control. For GLP-1-delayed meals (observed peaks 3–5 hours post-bolus), consider extended carbs or e-carb entries if meal timing is consistent, or rely on DIA 10 hours to account for prolonged absorption. Example: expecting 7 U for breakfast → deliver 1.5–2 U immediately at 08:00, allow SMB to deliver remaining 5–5.5 U over 2–4 hours. Establish correction bolus limits: trigger only if glucose >180 AND rising AND IOB <1 U; size 0.05–0.1 U per bolus, repeat every 15–30 min as needed instead of single large bolus.
primary_rec_title: Establish consistent meal bolus strategy: prebolus 0–15 min, immediate bolus 20–30% of total.
summary: 14-day closed-loop insulin pump (AAPS) and CGM telemetry from a user on GLP-1 therapy. Overall glucose control is reasonable (86% TIR, 121.6 mg/dL average) but marked by volatile afternoon peaks (up to 293 mg/dL) and two clusters of severe hypoglycemia (42–51 mg/dL on 08-13, 41–48 mg/dL on 08-14). Data quality is excellent (98.7% CGM coverage). No meal carbs logged; all meal insulin is delivered as SMB/UAM micro-boluses or minimal user boluses. Automated bolus strategy appears to lack a consistent prebolus and relies entirely on glucose-driven SMB/UAM feedback. Severe lows correlate with correction bolus oversizing during high IOB, not profile defects. Afternoon highs persist despite adequate SMB/UAM response, indicating meal bolus timing or sizing is the limiting factor. GLP-1 use (1.25 mg documented) is not reflected in profile adjustments (CR, DIA, or basal changes). Profile settings (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, target) are individually reasonable and do not require immediate changes. Automation (SMB/UAM, sensitivity limits, max IOB) is functioning as designed but cannot fully compensate for absent meal logging or inconsistent bolus strategy. Risk of recurrent hypoglycemia is moderate-to-high if correction bolus strategy continues without meal context.

meal_suggestion: Restore meal carb logging (daily entries for all meals: carb grams, time, macros). Implement prebolus 15 minutes before eating (user injects bolus covering ~50% of estimated carbs; loop SMB covers remainder during absorption). Reduce meal-detection threshold min_5m_carbimpact from 8 to 5 mg/dL/5 min to allow UAM to recognize slow-absorption meals (GLP-1 effect) and deploy appropriate meal-coverage insulin instead of basal adjustments. primary_rec_title: Restore meal carbohydrate logging
summary: A 14-day closed-loop T1DM dataset (98.7% CGM coverage) shows recurrent afternoon hyperglycemia (14:00–16:00, avg 148–163 mg/dL, TAR 23–32%) and evening hypoglycemia (19:00, TBR 15.3%, one min 41 mg/dL), with manageable but concerning safety profile (5.1% TBR overall, 5 critical lows <50 mg/dL; 8.9% TAR, 8 critical highs >280 mg/dL). Loop automation (SMB, UAM, Dynamic ISF) is well-configured and not the primary driver of observed patterns. The blocking issue is absent meal carbohydrate logging, which prevents validation of carb ratios, meal bolus adequacy, and absorption timing. Afternoon hyperglycemia is best explained by undersized or slowly-delivered meal bolus combined with a meal-detection threshold (min_5m_carbimpact 8 mg/dL/5 min) too high for slow-absorption meals (GLP-1 effect documented via 3 injections). Evening hypoglycemia follows afternoon correction overshoot amplified by increased basal rates and long DIA (10 h). Basal 0.5 U/h at 16:00 is low but not an isolated cause; improving meal detection and meal bolus strategy is prerequisite before basal revision. Primary recommendation: restore meal carb logging and reduce meal-detection threshold to 5 mg/dL/5 min. Secondary recommendations pending meal-log verification: implement 15-minute prebolus, review meal-specific absorption durations, and reassess Dynamic ISF aggressiveness (70% adjustment factor).

profile_rec_text: Increase Profile / basal 10:00 segment from 0.7 U/h to 0.8 U/h. Do not change other basal segments. Test this change for 3-7 days while monitoring midday BG (target avg 110-120 mg/dL, TIR >85%) and evening glucose (watch for lows emerging or worsening at hours 17-19 local). Overnight and early-morning basal (00:00-07:00) are stable and adequate; do not adjust.
meal_suggestion: Implement carb logging (timestamp + estimated grams for all meals) immediately as prerequisite. Current observed strategy is purely reactive: zero manual prebolus (all boluses fire 1-3 hours post-meal BG rise), no bolus split, no e-carbs, no meal carbs ever logged. Post-carb-logging (3-7 days): (1) Enable smb_with_cob_enabled=true to make SMB meal-aware, shifting bolus timing from 1-3 h post-peak to 0.5-1.5 h post-peak. (2) Test prebolus 5-10 minutes before next meal, comparing glucose response to current post-peak SMB. Measure reduction in midday peak BG. (3) Validate CR from logged carbs: if actual insulin/carb ratio differs from declared CR (10.5-13.2 g/U), adjust in profile (recommend 50-70% if system-wide ~4.6 inferred). (4) For GLP-1 injection days (Aug 14, 17, 20, and each week): either (A) reduce CR by 10% on injection day (e.g., CR 13.2→11.9), or (B) implement 2-h e-carbs for lunch/dinner if slow-meal rebound patterns (Aug 15 11:25 type) persist (log 50% carbs at meal, 50% as e-carb duration 2 h). (5) For evening lows (hours 17-19 local, min 41-42 mg/dL): increase evening basal (18:00) by +0.1 U/h OR reduce SMB interval (3→5 min) after midday-basal increase (recommendation 2) is tested; choose one, test separately, do not combine.
primary_rec_title: Implement carb logging immediately (prerequisite for all downstream optimizations)
summary: User has 86% time-in-range over 14 days with good CGM coverage (98.7%), but shows high variability (CoV 32.6%), consistent midday hyperglycemia (avg 132-163 mg/dL, hours 09-16 local), and evening lows (min 41-42 mg/dL, hours 18-19 local). The profile is incomplete in carb logging (zero entries over 14 days) and meal strategy documentation (empty meal_strategies array). Declared basal (0.5-0.8 U/h) appears insufficient for midday control; automation relies entirely on reactive SMB/UAM with no manual prebolus or carb-entry discipline. GLP-1 1.25 mg weekly (Aug 14, 17, 20) introduces appetite suppression and slower meal absorption unaddressed by static profile settings. Primary action: implement carb logging and increase midday basal segment, then evaluate meal strategy and evening low drivers.

profile_rec_text: Increase basal 10:00–17:00 segment from 0.7 to 0.85 U/h; remove or eliminate 16:00→17:00 local step-down from 0.7 to 0.5 U/h. Keep overnight basal (00:00–07:00) unchanged (0.6–0.8 U/h as currently profiled); re-assess after midday basal change effect is clear.
meal_suggestion: Transition from minimal immediate bolus (1–15%, current) + aggressive SMB/UAM primary coverage to hybrid meal coverage: adopt 15–30 min prebolus timing (all meals), 20–30% immediate bolus for standard meals (calculated via CR and logged carb estimate or rough 40–50g typical), and 30–40% immediate bolus for GLP-1 injection days (08-14, 08-17, 08-20 pattern; extend prebolus to 30–45 min to accommodate 30–90 min GLP-1 absorption delay). SMB/UAM will shift from primary meal-coverage engine (85–99% responsibility) to supportive fine-tuning role (10–30% of meal bolus, catching missed carbs or handling activity-induced sensitivity swings). For meals suspected of high fat content (extended absorption 3–4 hours), once meal carbs are logged, model 50–70% carbs as immediate bolus and 30–50% as extended-carb (e-carb) entry with 2–3 hour absorption window. This strategy decouples meal coverage from SMB frequency, reducing afternoon oscillation (current: under-bolus → late SMB ramp → over-correction crash) and improving early post-meal control (prevent 50–88 mg/dL rise within 60 min by pre-dosing). Rely on meal logging to enable CR validation and carb-ratio calibration; without logs, use conservative estimates ('breakfast ~40g, lunch ~45g, dinner ~50g, typical for adult T1D') and adjust after 3 meals based on observed glucose response.
primary_rec_title: Increase midday basal 10:00–17:00 from 0.7 to 0.85 U/h; eliminate 16:00 step-down to 0.5 U/h
summary: 14-day CGM and insulin delivery telemetry (2026-08-07 to 2026-08-21, 98.7% coverage) shows good overall control (86% time in range) but significant variability (CV 32.6%, SD 39.7 mg/dL) driven by bimodal glucose patterns: sustained midday highs (10:00–17:00 avg 132–162 mg/dL, peak 32% above range at 16:00) alternating with afternoon and early-night lows (16:00–18:00 and 23:00–03:00, 5–18% below range, min 41 mg/dL). Zero meal carbs logged; system relies entirely on basal, SMB/UAM, and unvalidated CR/ISF. Three GLP-1 injections (1.25 mg each on 08-14, 08-17, 08-20) correlate with worse-control days, indicating inadequate accommodation for delayed gastric emptying. User employs extreme minimum meal boluses (1–15% of calculated carbs) with primary reliance on SMB (3-min interval) and UAM (8 mg/dL/5 min threshold) for meal coverage. Observed therapy responses show clear under-correction cycles (minimal upfront bolus → late SMB ramp-up → rebound highs) and over-correction crashes (afternoon SMB micro-corrections and ISF boost dropping BG 100+ mg/dL in 2–4 hours). Root causes are (A) basal insufficiency midday (0.7 U/h at 10:00–16:00 vs. sustained 140+ mg/dL demand), (B) meal-bolus strategy mismatch with profile (1–15% immediate bolus, no prebolus, no e-carbs for delayed/extended absorption), and (C) profile-automation compensation (dynamic ISF 70% attempting to stabilize flat ISF 56; SMB over-tasked). One primary recommendation: increase basal 10:00–17:00 from 0.7 to 0.85 U/h to reduce midday high baseline and reliance on SMB, creating headroom for safer meal-bolus strategy and lower afternoon over-correction risk. Second priority: adopt prebolus and modest immediate bolus (20–30%) for all meals, especially GLP-1 days, decoupling meal coverage from SMB and improving stability. Third: log meal carbs and composition to enable profile validation. Implementation order: basal change first (verify effect 3–5 days), then meal-bolus strategy, then CR/ISF fine-tuning.

profile_rec_text: Reduce ISF from 56 mg/dL/U to 50 mg/dL/U. Do not change DIA, CR, or basal simultaneously. Observe for 2–3 days. After stabilization, add carb logs and meal bolus strategy (prebolus + at-meal) to address afternoon hyperglycemia and evening hypoglycemia caused by weak ISF + insufficient meal-bolus delivery.
meal_suggestion: Add explicit prebolus (10 minutes before meal, ~0.5–1 U for estimated 50 g carbs, representing ~30% of meal dose) followed by at-meal bolus (~1–2 U for lunch, 30% of meal dose). Allow SMB/UAM to deliver remaining ~40% via high temporary basal (3.2–4 U/h) and per-cycle micro-boluses over 1–2 hours. Continue standard 7-hour carbohydrate absorption model; e-carbs not indicated unless patient reports frequent high-fat meals (pizza, fatty meat). Prebolus front-loads insulin to match early carb rise; at-meal bolus begins active coverage before peak; SMB/UAM provide safety net and catch-up. Expected outcome: flatten afternoon glucose peaks from 160–180+ mg/dL to 130–150 mg/dL (reduce TAR 30–32% to 15–20%); reduce evening IOB overshoot (lower TBR from 15.3% to <10%); maintain overnight fasting control.
primary_rec_title: Add explicit prebolus and at-meal bolus to replace SMB-only meal coverage
summary: 14-day Nightscout/AAPS audit (Aug 7–21, 2026). CGM coverage 98.7%, data quality good. Overall glucose control: TIR 86%, moderate variability (CV 32.6%). Primary issues: afternoon hyperglycemia (TAR peak 32.1% at 15:00–17:00 local), evening hypoglycemia (TBR 15.3% at 19:00 local, 8 extremes ≤45 mg/dL). Root causes: (1) meal bolus strategy absent or minimal (5–10% of meal dose delivered at meal; 90–95% delegated to SMB/UAM); (2) profile ISF 56 mg/dL/U likely weak (corrections show variable efficacy; afternoon highs persist despite 3.2–4 U/h loop suggestions); (3) DIA 10h extends evening IOB, causing overshoot after large afternoon corrections. Overnight and morning fasting control are good; basal schedule is appropriate. No carb entries recorded; UAM detects meals late or incompletely. AAPS automation (SMB, UAM, max basal/IOB limits) is functioning appropriately and not constraining therapy; weakness is in profile settings and meal bolus execution. Recommendation: add explicit meal boluses (prebolus 10 min + 30% at-meal), evaluate ISF via carb logs, then confirm basal and target adjustments. Do not change dependent parameters (ISF + DIA, or CR + basal) simultaneously.

profile_rec_text: Reduce basal segment 00:00 UTC from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h to eliminate early-morning hypoglycemia (TBR 10–18% at 01:00–02:00 local). Verify this change over 3–5 days; monitor early-morning TBR (target <5%) and avg BG (target 99–110 mg/dL). Do not make other profile changes concurrently. After verification, proceed to carb logging and meal-bolus prebolus adjustment.
meal_suggestion: User is currently relying on AAPS SMB (every 3 min if BG elevated and IOB allows) for all meal bolusing, with no prebolus or e-carbs. This reactive strategy creates postprandial peaks (TARs 20–32%) because insulin delivery lags meal onset. Recommend: (1) After basal reduction (0.6 → 0.5 U/h at 00:00 UTC) is verified (3–5 days) and carb logging is established, add 5–10 min prebolus before recurring meals (morning ~08:00 local, afternoon ~14:00 local). Bolus size = meal carbs / CR (using AAPS meal wizard with logged carbs). (2) Continue SMB-only after prebolus (do not manually bolus meal carbs on top of SMB; let SMB fire every 3 min). (3) E-carbs are not indicated until meal composition is known from carb logs; once slow-absorbing meals are identified (high fat, high fiber), e-carbs can be designed for 2–4 hour absorption if needed. (4) Carb logging is mandatory and must begin immediately (concurrent with basal verification) to unlock meal detection (COB > 0), CR validation, and meal-bolus optimization.
primary_rec_title: Reduce early-morning basal 00:00 UTC from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h
summary: User has good CGM coverage (98.7%) and AAPS automation is configured conservatively and appropriately. Primary issue is early-morning hypoglycemia (01:00–02:00 local, TBR 10–18%) linked to basal 0.6 U/h at 00:00 UTC being too aggressive for that time window. Secondary issues are afternoon hyperglycemia (14:00–17:00 local, TARs 23–32%) and postprandial peaks (TARs 20%) caused by meal detection failure (zero carb logs; UAM cannot infer meals with gradient <8 mg/dL per 5 min). AAPS SMB, DIA, max basal, max IOB, and automation sensitivity settings are appropriate and not defective. No automation tuning is needed. The meal strategy is reactive (SMB-only, no prebolus, no e-carbs, no carb logs); meal bolusing cannot be optimized until carb logging begins. One clear profile change is supported: reduce basal 00:00 UTC from 0.6 to 0.5 U/h to eliminate early-morning lows. This change must be verified over 3–5 days before any other tuning. Carb logging is mandatory to unblock CR, ISF, and meal-bolus strategy validation.

profile_rec_text: Increase basal rate at 16:00 (local time segment) from 0.5 U/h to 0.8 U/h. This addresses the primary driver of afternoon hyperglycemia (hour 16 worst outcome, avg 162.8 mg/dL, TAR 32.1%). Implement as a single sequential change. Monitor hour 16–17 glucose closely for 3–5 days. If lows worsen (hour 01 TBR increasing above 18.5% or new lows appearing post-basal increase), verify that overnight basal 0.6 U/h at 00:00 is appropriate and that hour 01 lows are not basal-driven (likely post-meal IOB, not basal insufficiency, given basal 0.6 is modest and overnight TIR is strong at 81.5–98.7% elsewhere). After basal response is confirmed, verify carb logging with 1 full day before considering CR or Dynamic ISF adjustments.
meal_suggestion: Patient is using a reactive micro-bolus (0.05–0.25 U delivered at or during meal rise, 0 min prebolus) combined with AAPS automatic SMB/UAM delivery (3-min interval, 0.125 U/15 min basal-equivalent cap, COB estimated via 8 mg/dL/5 min rise threshold). Total meal insulin over 30–120 min is approximately 0.3–1.0 U. No e-carbs are declared or used; carb absorption is modeled via AAPS COB estimation with meal_max_absorption 7 h and DIA 10 h. This strategy is appropriate for closed-loop automation and reduces carb-logging burden. However, absence of carb entries prevents validation of bolus proportionality. Recommend: (1) maintain current reactive micro-bolus strategy (do not prebolus; timing is reactive-appropriate); (2) immediately log 1 full day of meal carbs (breakfast, lunch, dinner) to validate whether bolus sizes are proportional to carbs or intentionally conservative; (3) after carb logging, if bolus sizes are proportional to carbs and CR is appropriate, maintain strategy unchanged; (4) if basal increase (16:00 from 0.5 to 0.8 U/h) reduces afternoon hyperglycemia as expected and IOB remains elevated (>6 U), consider reducing meal_max_absorption to 4–5 h to improve COB decay without changing bolus strategy itself.
primary_rec_title: Increase basal from 0.5 U/h to 0.8 U/h at 16:00 local segment.
